nodes.text: Build me a sparse, atmospheric medieval mountain fortress occupying a rocky rise beside a broad, shallow, muddy river or flooded plain, surrounded by rolling green-and-tan terrain and steep, pale, heavily eroded mountains. Place one large ruined stone castle at one end of the scene, formed from a compact cluster of adjoining structures: a tall rectangular gatehouse or keep with a pointed-arched opening, several lower round and square towers, crenellated curtain walls, roofless interior chambers, broken wall sections, and scattered red banners and small red-tiled or conical roofs. Extend a long, straight fortified stone bridge or causeway outward from the castle across the water, lined with low battlements and supported by a repeated sequence of broad masonry arches; terminate its far end with a small roofed gateway-like section. Beside the castle end, add a damaged wooden ramp, stairs, platforms, braces, and numerous irregular vertical piles emerging from the water, some leaning or broken. Scatter a few isolated posts and debris across the flooded area, but keep the composition largely open and uncluttered. Set pale boulders around the castle foundations and patches of vivid low vegetation along the shoreline, with one or two dense dark-green tree clusters near the bridge’s outer side. Shape the surrounding ground as broad undulating slopes, exposed cream-colored ridges, shallow channels, and distant water edges, using strongly rippled terrain surfaces. Keep the fortress and bridge as the only major built elements, with generous empty space emphasizing their isolation, ruined condition, and dramatic scale under warm low sunlight, long shadows, and a partly cloudy sky.

graph.prompt:
Build me a sparse, atmospheric medieval mountain fortress occupying a rocky rise beside a broad, shallow, muddy river or flooded plain, surrounded by rolling green-and-tan terrain and steep, pale, heavily eroded mountains. Place one large ruined stone castle at one end of the scene, formed from a compact cluster of adjoining structures: a tall rectangular gatehouse or keep with a pointed-arched opening, several lower round and square towers, crenellated curtain walls, roofless interior chambers, broken wall sections, and scattered red banners and small red-tiled or conical roofs. Extend a long, straight fortified stone bridge or causeway outward from the castle across the water, lined with low battlements and supported by a repeated sequence of broad masonry arches; terminate its far end with a small roofed gateway-like section. Beside the castle end, add a damaged wooden ramp, stairs, platforms, braces, and numerous irregular vertical piles emerging from the water, some leaning or broken. Scatter a few isolated posts and debris across the flooded area, but keep the composition largely open and uncluttered. Set pale boulders around the castle foundations and patches of vivid low vegetation along the shoreline, with one or two dense dark-green tree clusters near the bridge’s outer side. Shape the surrounding ground as broad undulating slopes, exposed cream-colored ridges, shallow channels, and distant water edges, using strongly rippled terrain surfaces. Keep the fortress and bridge as the only major built elements, with generous empty space emphasizing their isolation, ruined condition, and dramatic scale under warm low sunlight, long shadows, and a partly cloudy sky.

    over empty space -- which is a failed reconstruction no matter how good
    the massing is. These palette entries are also flat surfaces you can tile

deterministic_rule_draft.prompt: Build me a sparse, atmospheric medieval mountain fortress occupying a rocky rise beside a broad, shallow, muddy river or flooded plain, surrounded by rolling green-and-tan terrain and steep, pale, heavily eroded mountains. Place one large ruined stone castle at one end of the scene, formed from a compact cluster of adjoining structures: a tall rectangular gatehouse or keep with a pointed-arched opening, several lower round and square towers, crenellated curtain walls, roofless interior chambers, broken wall sections, and scattered red banners and small red-tiled or conical roofs. Extend a long, straight fortified stone bridge or causeway outward from the castle across the water, lined with low battlements and supported by a repeated sequence of broad masonry arches; terminate its far end with a small roofed gateway-like section. Beside the castle end, add a damaged wooden ramp, stairs, platforms, braces, and numerous irregular vertical piles emerging from the water, some leaning or broken. Scatter a few isolated posts and debris across the flooded area, but keep the composition largely open and uncluttered. Set pale boulders around the castle foundations and patches of vivid low vegetation along the shoreline, with one or two dense dark-green tree clusters near the bridge’s outer side. Shape the surrounding ground as broad undulating slopes, exposed cream-colored ridges, shallow channels, and distant water edges, using strongly rippled terrain surfaces. Keep the fortress and bridge as the only major built elements, with generous empty space emphasizing their isolation, ruined condition, and dramatic scale under warm low sunlight, long shadows, and a partly cloudy sky.

major_clause_coverage.source_text: Build me a sparse, atmospheric medieval mountain fortress occupying a rocky rise beside a broad, shallow, muddy river or flooded plain, surrounded by rolling green-and-tan terrain and steep, pale, heavily eroded mountains.

Place one large ruined stone castle at one end of the scene, formed from a compact cluster of adjoining structures: a tall rectangular gatehouse or keep with a pointed-arched opening, several lower round and square towers, crenellated curtain walls, roofless interior chambers, broken wall sections, and scattered red banners and small red-tiled or conical roofs.

Extend a long, straight fortified stone bridge or causeway outward from the castle across the water, lined with low battlements and supported by a repeated sequence of broad masonry arches; terminate its far end with a small roofed gateway-like section.
Beside the castle end, add a damaged wooden ramp, stairs, platforms, braces, and numerous irregular vertical piles emerging from the water, some leaning or broken.
Scatter a few isolated posts and debris across the flooded area, but keep the composition largely open and uncluttered.
Set pale boulders around the castle foundations and patches of vivid low vegetation along the shoreline, with one or two dense dark-green tree clusters near the bridge’s outer side.
Shape the surrounding ground as broad undulating slopes, exposed cream-colored ridges, shallow channels, and distant water edges, using strongly rippled terrain surfaces.

Keep the fortress and bridge as the only major built elements, with generous empty space emphasizing their isolation, ruined condition, and dramatic scale under warm low sunlight, long shadows, and a partly cloudy sky.
